afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 271831 AAA
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
Issued by National Weather Service Tucson AZ
1130 AM MST Sun Sep 27 2026

...UPDATED FOR AVIATION SECTION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A band of light rain will impact portions of the region later
  today and into Monday before more scattered showers and
  thunderstorms become possible starting Monday afternoon.

- A Flood Watch has been issued for Monday night and much of
  Tuesday for higher terrain areas of central and eastern Arizona.
  Moderate to heavy rainfall may also impact portions of the
  Arizona lower deserts, but we are expecting it to be much more
  localized.

- Near to below normal temperatures are expected through the
  middle part of the week before warming to slightly above normal
  by next weekend.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
The main forecast concern continues to be the potential for
widespread rainfall, particularly from late Monday through Tuesday
afternoon. Unfortunately, model guidance is still showing a good
deal of uncertainty with the timing and track of the incoming
Pacific low and how it will interact with the influx of moisture
through Monday. Current satellite imagery shows high level clouds
streaming into our region from the fast decaying TC Odalys well to
our southwest, while a much better organized TC Polo is slowly
drifting northward toward southern Baja. Even the forecast for
later today is a bit tricky as the higher level moisture from
Odalys will begin to interact with the incoming Pacific trough
which is approaching northern California.

We anticipate a continuous feed of higher level moisture from the
southwest for the rest of today and likely lasting into early
Monday morning. As this occurs, the moisture will gradually shift
more into the mid-levels due to top-down saturating of the layers.
There is also model evidence of some weak to moderate ascent
within the saturated layer prompting showers to begin to develop
later this morning. CAMs generally agree on increasing light
shower coverage later this morning, but most of this will not
reach the surface as the sub-cloud layer is starting out very dry.
This band of showers should eventually moisten the lower levels
enough by later this afternoon into this evening to allow for some
off and on light rain somewhere from southeast California through
southwest Arizona into around the Phoenix area. This rain is not
likely to amount to much, but most locations within this swath
should at least measure a few hundredths to maybe a tenth of an
inch. Some guidance shows a very narrow (25-50 miles maybe) of
amounts upward of a quarter inch from this evening through
tonight, which seems reasonable if it stays over the same area for
6-12 hours. We also can't rule amounts upwards of 0.50" closer to
the mountains in northwest Maricopa County. The atmosphere should
remain quite stable through Monday morning, so we are at most
expecting a few rumbles of thunder.

Model trends over the past 24 hours has shown a little faster
progression of the Pacific low as it moves through our region
later Monday through Tuesday, as well as slightly less available
moisture. This still does not mean heavy rainfall will not happen,
it just means it will most likely be more confined to higher
terrain areas north and east of Phoenix and a more localized. The
center of the low is forecast to move into southern California by
Monday evening with increasing forced ascent during the latter
half of Monday and continuing through the first half of Tuesday.
The strongest forcing is expected just out ahead of the low
center, focused over the western deserts Monday afternoon/evening
and then progressing through southern and central Arizona Monday
night through Tuesday afternoon.

After the initial swath of light rain tapers off at some time
Monday afternoon, we are expecting scattered showers and
thunderstorms to develop somewhere along the Lower CO River Valley
late afternoon before slowly tracking eastward through southwest
Arizona in the evening/early overnight hours. A few of these
storms may end up being strong with potential for an isolated
severe storm too. Additional scattered showers with embedded
weaker storms are likely to impact higher terrain areas in Arizona
later on Monday before becoming more widespread at some point
Monday night and/or Tuesday morning. The timing is still a bit
uncertain, but the peak time frame for rainfall for central and
eastern Arizona looks to be between 3 AM Tuesday through Tuesday
afternoon. A Flood Watch has been issued for the foothills areas
of northern Maricopa County, northern and eastern portions of the
Phoenix metro and for the higher terrain northeast and east of
Phoenix. The Watch will be in effect from midnight Monday night
through the first part of Tuesday evening. Guidance generally
agrees the low will begin to exit the area to the east Tuesday
night with any shower activity winding down from west to east
during the evening/early overnight hours.

QPF amounts have gone down some from previous forecasts with
rainfall amounts averaging from around 0.1" in the Lower CO River
Valley to 0.35-0.75" for the lower deserts of south-central
Arizona. Higher amounts are expected within the Watch area,
averaging between 1.0-1.25", but localized amounts of 2-3" will
be possible. Keep in mind, there is still a good amount of spread
among the models for anticipated rainfall amounts and these
average expected amounts could still easily go up or down some.

As far as the strong to severe storm threat, the faster timing of
the system is leading to less of a severe storm threat. Forecast
instability remains the main issue with CAPE not likely getting
much above 500 J/kg. However, even with roughly 500 or maybe 750
J/kg, this may be enough to allow for a few stronger and maybe
even an isolated severe storm on Tuesday as the low center moves
eastward through central Arizona. As of right now, this limited
risk of severe storms is likely to stay across far southern into
southeast Arizona from late Tuesday morning through Tuesday
afternoon.

&&

.LONG TERM /WEDNESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Upper level ridging is forecast to quickly surge in from the west
on Wednesday leaving clearing skies and lowering surface moisture
through Thursday. Temperatures for the coming week will stay
somewhat stable across the western lower deserts, but still on
average slightly below normal today through Tuesday. Much cooler
temperatures are expected for most of Arizona with highs only in
the 80s for the Phoenix area Monday-Wednesday. Once the ridging
moves in from the west later this week, temperatures will creep
upward again with highs topping 100 degrees across the western
deserts by Thursday or Friday and potentially for the Phoenix area
by next weekend.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1830Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:

The main weather concern will be the increasing chance for SHRA and 
at some points erratic winds. Confidence is low in the exact timing 
for direct impacts to the terminals, however the general outlook is 
VCSH later tonight before a thicker band of -SHRA begins to filter 
in over the metro by tomorrow morning. Latest guidance shows 
activity lingering through most of the back half of the TAF package, 
however further analysis will be needed. The remainder of this 
afternoon can expect diurnal trends, before a NW/NNW direction is 
expected to develop for the overnight periods, where gusts into a 15-
25kt range cannot be ruled out tonight as a result of nearby shower 
activity. BKN-OVC cloud decks with bases aoa 10kft are expected to 
be common through the TAF period, while FEW-SCT lower decks are 
likely to develop tomorrow morning during showers.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:

The main aviation concern will be the possibility of VCSH/SHRA 
mostly at KIPL, however KBLH may also be affected. Confidence is low 
in the exact timing of impacts, but the best timing for VCSH/SHRA to 
start is near 12Z tomorrow morning. KIPL can expect typical diurnal 
tendencies fluctuating between SW and SE. At KBLH, any rain in the 
morning and afternoon is expected to remain to the south and east of 
the terminal. BKN/OVC high clouds will continue with FEW-SCT mid 
level clouds.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Moisture will increase across the area today and Monday with
light rain developing this evening followed by locally moderate
to heavy rainfall with thunderstorm chances later Monday into
Tuesday. The bulk of the expected rainfall will favor the eastern
districts. Min RHs today will dip to 20-30% this afternoon before
improving to 40-60% over much of the area for Monday and Tuesday.
Winds through Monday will generally follow the typical diurnal
tendencies, but with a tendency to favor the south. A front moving
through the area on Tuesday will turn winds out of the west
northwest with gusty winds of 20-30 mph possible across the
western districts. Drier conditions and near to slightly above
normal temperatures are forecast for later this week.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Flood Watch from late Monday night through Tuesday evening for
     AZZ534-537-541-542-545-547-549-552-555>558-560>563.

CA...None.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Kuhlman
LONG TERM...Kuhlman
AVIATION...Whittock
FIRE WEATHER...Kuhlman
